content: 1. Linezolid is strongly recommended for inclusion in the treatment regimens of patients with multidrug-resistant or rifampicin-resistant tuberculosis (MDR/RR-TB) undergoing longer treatment courses. This recommendation is based on moderate certainty of evidence. 2. Clofazimine and cycloserine (or terizidone) may be included in the treatment regimens of MDR/RR-TB patients on longer regimens. This is a conditional recommendation with very low certainty of evidence. 3. Ethambutol may be included in the treatment regimens of MDR/RR-TB patients on longer regimens. This is a conditional recommendation with very low certainty of evidence. 4. Delamanid may be included in the treatment regimens of MDR/RR-TB patients aged 3 years or older on longer regimens. This is a conditional recommendation with moderate certainty of evidence. 5. In children under 3 years of age with MDR/RR-TB, delamanid may be used as part of longer regimens. This is a new and additional conditional recommendation with very low certainty of evidence. 6. Pyrazinamide may be included in the treatment regimens of MDR/RR-TB patients on longer regimens. This is a conditional recommendation with very low certainty of evidence. 7. Imipenem-cilastatin or meropenem may be included in the treatment regimens of MDR/RR-TB patients on longer regimens. This is a conditional recommendation with very low certainty of evidence. 8. Amikacin may be included in the treatment regimens of MDR/RR-TB patients aged 18 years or older on longer regimens, provided susceptibility has been demonstrated and adequate measures to monitor for adverse reactions are ensured. If amikacin is unavailable, streptomycin may replace it under the same conditions. This is a conditional recommendation with very low certainty of evidence. 9. Ethionamide or prothionamide may only be included in the treatment regimens of MDR/RR-TB patients on longer regimens if bedaquiline, linezolid, clofazimine, or delamanid are not used, or if better options to compose a regimen are not possible. This is a conditional recommendation against use, with very low certainty of evidence. 10. Clavulanic acid should not be included in the treatment regimens of MDR/RR-TB patients on longer regimens. This is a strong recommendation against use, with low certainty of evidence. 11. For MDR/RR-TB patients on longer regimens, a total treatment duration of 18–20 months is suggested for most patients. The duration may be modified based on the patient’s response to therapy. This is a conditional recommendation with very low certainty of evidence. 12. For MDR/RR-TB patients on longer regimens, a treatment duration of 15–17 months after culture conversion is suggested for most patients. The duration may be modified based on the patient’s response to therapy. This is a conditional recommendation with very low certainty of evidence. 13. For MDR/RR-TB patients on longer regimens containing amikacin or streptomycin, an intensive phase of 6–7 months is suggested for most patients. The duration may be modified based on the patient’s response to therapy. This is a conditional recommendation with very low certainty of evidence. 14. In MDR/RR-TB patients on longer regimens, sputum culture in addition to sputum smear microscopy is recommended to monitor treatment response. Monthly repetition of sputum culture is desirable. This is a strong recommendation with moderate certainty in the estimates of test accuracy. 15. Antiretroviral therapy is recommended for all patients with HIV and drug-resistant tuberculosis requiring second-line antituberculosis drugs, regardless of CD4 cell count. It should be initiated as early as possible, ideally within the first 8 weeks following the start of antituberculosis treatment. This is a strong recommendation with very low certainty of evidence. 16. In patients with rifampicin-resistant tuberculosis (RR-TB) or multidrug-resistant tuberculosis (MDR-TB), elective partial lung resection (lobectomy or wedge resection) may be used alongside a recommended MDR-TB regimen. This is a conditional recommendation with very low certainty of evidence. 17. Care and support for patients with MDR/RR-TB are addressed in a separate sub-module of the WHO consolidated guidelines on tuberculosis, specifically Module 4: Treatment – Tuberculosis care and support. 18. In patients with confirmed rifampicin-susceptible and isoniazid-resistant tuberculosis (Hr-TB), treatment with rifampicin, ethambutol, pyrazinamide, and levofloxacin is recommended for a duration of 6 months. This is a conditional recommendation with very low certainty of evidence. 19. In patients with confirmed rifampicin-susceptible and isoniazid-resistant tuberculosis, it is not recommended to add streptomycin or other injectable agents to the treatment regimen. This is a conditional recommendation with very low certainty of evidence.
